key_insight: A unified crystal plasticity-fracture model shows that creep cracking shifts from transgranular at high stress to intergranular at low stress because slip-driven intragranular cracking competes with grain-boundary cavitation.
engineering_relevance: This mechanism explains how stress level controls creep rupture mode, ductility, and life in polycrystalline metals, helping guide high-temperature alloy design and damage prediction.
method: Crystal plasticity coupled with grain-boundary cavitation
Crystallographic crack propagation to capture intra- and intergranular damage
evidence_signal: Microscale simulations reproduce a stress-dependent transition in crack paths and damage localization, linking high-stress ductile rupture to low-stress quasi-brittle rupture.
watch_item: The framework is computationally detailed and material-specific, so calibration and validation against experiments are likely necessary before broad design use.
paper_title: Mechanistic transition between inter- and trans-granular creep cracking via a unified crystal plasticity-fracture framework
